examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Decide whether order matters, repetition is allowed, objects are distinguishable, and empty selections are permitted. Use complementary counting for ‘at least one’ and inclusion–exclusion for overlapping forbidden events. Stars and bars counts nonnegative integer solutions, not arrangements of distinguishable individual items.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
How many nonnegative integer solutions satisfy x1+x2+x3+x4=7?

**Answer: 120.** Represent seven units as stars and choose positions for three dividers among ten symbols. Count=binomial(7+4−1,4−1)=binomial(10,3)=120. Zero-valued variables correspond to adjacent dividers or dividers at the ends.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
For positive variables first subtract 1 from each, reducing the total by the number of variables. Do not use the nonnegative formula unchanged.

Do not use a permutation when the order of the selected objects is irrelevant.
